key_insight: In Fe-doped, oxygen-deficient SrTiO3(001), the OER activity depends strongly on defect charge state and Fermi level, with neutral Fe being nearly benign but reduced Fe and some oxygen vacancies causing large overpotentials.
engineering_relevance: Defect and Fermi-level engineering can be used to predict whether dopants or vacancies will help or hurt catalytic performance in perovskite oxide electrodes.
method: DFT calculations of charge-dependent defect formation energies, segregation energies, and charge transition levels
Computational hydrogen electrode analysis of OER free-energy profiles on TiO2-terminated SrTiO3(001)
Comparison of pristine, Fe-doped, and oxygen-vacancy states across relevant Fermi-level conditions
evidence_signal: The abstract reports overpotentials ranging from 0.43-0.48 V for neutral Fe and pristine surfaces up to 1.35 V for reduced Fe states, while oxygen vacancies span from 0.45 V to 2.13 V depending on charge state and site.
watch_item: The conclusions are based on first-principles surface models, so real interfaces may differ due to temperature, kinetics, and non-ideal defect distributions.
paper_title: Fermi-Level-Dependent Defect Chemistry and Oxygen Evolution Reaction Activity of Fe-Doped and Oxygen-Deficient \ce{SrTiO3}(001)
